claim: Oracle's full-time headcount fell from about 162,000 (about 58,000 in the US) at 31 May 2025 to about 141,000 (about 49,000 in the US) at 31 May 2026.

evidence.quote: As of May 31, 2025, we employed approximately 162,000 full-time employees, of which approximately 58,000 were employed in the U.S.
As of May 31, 2026, we employed approximately 141,000 full-time employees, of which approximately 49,000 were employed in the U.S. and approximately 92,000 were employed internationally.

claim: Oracle's restructuring and other expenses were $1,838 million in fiscal 2026 versus $374 million in fiscal 2025; the 2026 Restructuring Plan was estimated at up to $2.1 billion as of 31 August 2026, and management then added about $700 million for further actions.

evidence.quote: Restructuring and other expenses increased by $1.5 billion in reported currency in fiscal 2026 relative to fiscal 2025 primarily due to higher restructuring expenses
Subsequent to August 31, 2026, our management supplemented the 2026 Restructuring Plan by approximately $ 700 million to reflect additional actions that we expect to take.

claim: Compensia was the Oracle Compensation Committee's independent compensation advisor for fiscal 2026, reported directly to the committee and provided no other services to Oracle in fiscal 2026.

evidence.quote: The Compensation Committee retained Compensia, a national compensation consulting firm, as its independent compensation advisor for fiscal 2026
Compensia reports directly to the Compensation Committee and Compensia did not provide any other services to Oracle during fiscal 2026.

claim: Oracle's 2025 say-on-pay proposal received about 82% of votes cast; the Compensation Committee (Awo Ablo, Charles W. Moorman as Chair, Stephen H. Rusckowski) also oversees human capital matters including talent acquisition and retention.

evidence.quote: Stockholders approved our advisory say-on-pay proposal at our 2025 Annual Meeting with approximately 82% of the votes cast voting in favor of the compensation of our NEOs
Compensation Committee has general oversight over human capital matters, including talent acquisition and retention

claim: Oracle's fiscal 2026 10-K says AI adoption has resulted, and may continue to result, in workforce reductions, and that restructurings may lead to shortages of skilled employees and damage to morale and retention.

evidence.quote: The adoption and deployment of AI technologies across our operations have resulted, and may continue to result, in reductions to our workforce,
These types of restructurings may also lead to shortages of sufficiently skilled employees in certain roles, loss of valuable institutional knowledge and damage to employee morale and retention.
